news.casting_brief: NASA astrophysics director, scrappy startup engineers and founder, rival aerospace bidders, mission controllers; high-stakes underdog dynamic racing a clock against orbital decay.
news.script_brief: NASA gambles a $500M dying observatory on a 2020 startup who pitched the only plausible plan. In under a year, Katalyst must build, launch, and chase Swift, then latch with three robotic arms to boost its orbit. Tension: untested tech, tight budget, falling satellite. Hooks: the pitch, the contract, the catch.
news.news_close_brief: Katalyst's Link spacecraft must reach Swift and haul it back to a safe altitude before the astronomy mission falls to Earth. Whether the daring rescue succeeds remains to be seen.

dramatic_state.dramatic_question: Will Katalyst's Link spacecraft latch its three robotic arms onto Swift in time to boost the dying observatory's orbit?
dramatic_state.character_a_wants: Launch Katalyst's untested Link spacecraft within the year to catch and boost the falling Swift.
dramatic_state.character_b_wants: Ground Link until the three robotic arms are proven, refusing to gamble $500M on raw tech.
dramatic_state.ending_change: Link reaches Swift over Wallops' horizon; the three arms grip, and the $500M observatory rises instead of burning up.

rendered_lines: When Swift begins to fall only the bold plan from startup Katalyst offers NASA any hope of rescue.
That gauge needle's sliding again, Peter. Half a billion if the whole bird's lost by morning and you're the one holding the call.
The arm's never left the crate. If we cut it loose anyway, what's the reach before it misses?
Latch won't give past two-point-eight before the fuel line starves, and that needle keeps walking its own path.
Five hundred million already spent on the only deep-field readings this decade, and the crate stays right where it sits.
The chaser's AI never cleared a radiation check on that crate, and the needle's not waiting.
Run the test sequence before anyone touches the board again.
That sequence dumps the whole downlink into the backup log.
You been piping those readings to Langley while the rest of us watch the needle twitch?
Both outfits want the same window, Lemmy, but somebody's got to decide whose log stays live.
Sequence's running. The crate lifts in four minutes whether the checks clear or not.
Langley pulled the trigger on that vector the second the needle held steady.
The crate won't wait on anybody's decision now.
The needle stayed right where Langley put it, but the price for that kind of fix never gets any smaller.
Might as well wipe the glass clean before it starts all over again.
Katalyst's Link spacecraft must now reach Swift in time to raise its orbit before the mission ends in flames. Whether the rescue succeeds remains unknown.
